title: Kenya's Homecoming Push: Journey Back to Eden, $5.04bn Remittances, a Slowdown | The Six, Ep. 27
lede: Kenya is courting its diaspora and the wider African diaspora with visa-free entry for Africans, a 2024 diaspora policy and Journey Back to Eden, a relocation programme launched in Nairobi in December 2025. At the same time, remittances, a record $5.04 billion in 2025, are on course for their first annual fall in 17 years.
keyPoints: Kenyans abroad sent home a record $5.04 billion in 2025, up 1.9%, the weakest growth in more than 15 years (CBK via ITWeb and Nation).

Through October 2026, inflows were Sh545.8 billion ($4.19 billion), down Sh1.8 billion on a year earlier; to avoid the first annual fall since 2009, about $437 million a month is needed in November and December (Nation).

From January to October, US inflows fell to $1.96 billion from $2.29 billion and Saudi inflows to $132.5 million from $268.9 million; CBK Governor Kamau Thugge attributes the slowdown to those two corridors (Nation; Capital FM).
Journey Back to Eden, launched in December 2025 by the government and the African American-owned firm Traverze Culture, offers 7- and 12-day relocation and investment trips (TV47; Business Today).
A central bank survey found households received KSh931.8 billion in remittances from June 2024 to May 2025; for 22.3% of recipients it is their main livelihood (CBK).
